title: Pop Culture Digest — Friday, October 23, 2026
description:
Friday · October 23, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Friday’s conversation: tributes for Alien and Top Gun star Tom Skerritt, who died at 93, RAYE winning the Mercury Prize over Paul McCartney and Olivia Dean, all of Nobody Wants This Season 3 landing on Netflix, and Judi Dench saying her eyesight means she can no longer act.
Movies

Tom Skerritt, the captain in Alien and Viper in Top Gun, dies at 93

Tom Skerritt died Wednesday of natural causes at his home in Seattle, his family said. Over six decades he became Hollywood’s go-to steady authority figure: Dallas, the doomed captain of the Nostromo in Alien (he was billed first, ahead of Sigourney Weaver), Commander Mike “Viper” Metcalf telling Tom Cruise’s class they were “the top 1% of all naval aviators” in Top Gun, and the Presbyterian minister father of Brad Pitt and Craig Sheffer in A River Runs Through It.

He won a lead actor Emmy in 1993 as the small-town sheriff on David E. Kelley’s Picket Fences, and his credits also include M*A*S*H, Steel Magnolias, Contact and Ted. “While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives,” his family said.

Top Gun trailer on YouTube →   ·   Variety →   ·   CBS News →

Music

RAYE wins the Mercury Prize, beating Paul McCartney and Olivia Dean

RAYE took the 2026 Mercury Prize Thursday night in Newcastle for This Music May Contain Hope, her No. 1 second album with the hit “Where Is My Husband!” She then performed “I Hate The Way I Look Today” to a standing ovation. Judges praised how the album moves through jazz, soul, R&B and classical to show “what an album can be.”

It’s her first win after her 2023 debut was also shortlisted, and she’s the first solo woman to win since Little Simz in 2022. The shortlist included Olivia Dean’s chart-topping The Art of Loving and Paul McCartney’s The Boys of Dungeon Lane, his first-ever Mercury nomination. The prize comes with £25,000.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Billboard →

Streaming

Nobody Wants This Season 3 is out, and critics say it’s a rebound

All 10 episodes of the Kristen Bell and Adam Brody rom-com dropped on Netflix Thursday, and reviews are warmer than they were for Season 2. Joanne and Noah have moved in together, her ex (Avan Jogia) turns out to live next door, and the season finally leans into the spark between Morgan and Sasha. IndieWire gave it a B+, calling it fizzy fun with a darker streak of self-sabotage, and early Rotten Tomatoes reviews were all positive.

Miley Cyrus fans have a reason to watch too: the soundtrack, out today, includes a demo of her long-shelved ballad “Cold Blooded” and a stripped-down version of “You.” The new season lands as Netflix deals with a weak forecast and a drop in its stock.

Nobody Wants This Season 3 trailer on YouTube →   ·   IndieWire →

Celebrities

Judi Dench says her sight loss means she can no longer act

“I can’t be on stage. I can’t do a play anymore. I can’t do a film anymore. I can’t read anymore,” Judi Dench, 91, told BBC Radio 4’s Today program. She was diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration in 2012 and says she now struggles to recognize faces, sometimes giving strangers “an almost hug” by mistake.

The Oscar winner for Shakespeare in Love and longtime Bond boss M kept the interview light, telling stories about lunch with a former MI6 chief and meeting Sidney Poitier, and saying she’s still “besotted” with Shakespeare’s sonnets. Asked who should be the next Bond, she simply said “no.”

BBC News →

Bottom of the news

  • Clayface pulled an estimated $3.5 million-plus in Thursday previews, with Deadline’s weekend forecasts at $20–25 million.
  • BLACKPINK’s LISA released her first solo EP, Press Play, led by “SaWaDiKa” and “Tarantino,” ahead of her Las Vegas residency in November.
  • Kacey Musgraves announced Middle of Nowhere, Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes for Jan. 15 and released “Weekend In Texas” and “Mi Tesoro.”
  • Netflix shares fell about 5% after a weak forecast and a cut to its ad-sales outlook, and Ted Sarandos admitted “we could do better.”
  • Prime Video renewed Mike Flanagan’s Carrie for a second season after it hit No. 1 in more than 105 countries.
  • Michael Gray, star of the 1970s Shazam! TV series, died at 75.
  • Tom Hanks and Kelli O’Hara will bring This World of Tomorrow to Broadway in fall 2027.
  • Keanu Reeves is in talks to star in James Wan’s The Gangster, The Cop, The Devil at Paramount.
